answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral and tracks equivocation across the graph: if k identities coordinate a conflicting claim, correlated penalties grow as O(k^2), rather than linearly. Detection then applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier to the controlling stake, while asymmetric depreciation prevents recovery through account replacement. Thus a sybil vine cannot forge consensus or use an inlet identity to dilute accountability.
